messages:
maya (Support): Hi @kevin — sorry for the trouble. Can you capture a HAR + console logs for the flow that shows the API 502/timeout? We just need the network HAR (with response bodies) and console output. Please also grab the request-id from the failing request so we can correlate with backend logs.

kevin (Customer): Yep I can reproduce. Steps: click Sign in -> enter creds -> press Continue -> UI hangs and shows "Something went wrong" after ~10s. Where in the network tab should I look for the request-id?

maya (Support): Thanks. Quick checklist: (1) Open DevTools (Chrome: F12) -> Network tab -> check "Preserve log" -> reproduce the failure -> right-click on any request -> "Save all as HAR with content". (2) Switch to Console tab -> copy console text (right click -> Save as). (3) Search the HAR for headers like "x-request-id", "request-id", or "x-redwood-reqid". That header value is the request id we need. If you can't find it, copy the full response headers for the failing request and paste here.

kevin (Customer): I found a header: X-Request-Id: 01H8QWZ2KX-000a. Uploading HAR now.

julian (Eng): Nice — thanks. A few helpful extras if possible: include the full request/response bodies for the failing call, and the exact timestamp (UTC) when you hit the failing action (we'll search logs +/- 1 minute). If you want to produce a curl repro, here's a sanitized pattern you can use (do NOT paste your real Authorization header in public channels):

```bash
# example (replace URL and payload as appropriate)
curl -v \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: 01H8QWZ2KX-000a" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"test"}' \n  'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate'
```

sarah (SRE): Two quick hygiene notes: 1) redact Authorization, Cookie, and any other PII before uploading. 2) If you prefer a safe, auto-sanitized HAR export we can provide a pre-signed upload link to our support portal — DM me and I'll generate it.

julian (Eng): If the HAR is already uploaded, here's a one-liner to pull X-Request-Id values locally: 

```bash
jq -r '.log.entries[].request.headers[] | select(.name|ascii_downcase=="x-request-id") | .value' mycapture.har
```

maya (Support): Also, if the user is on Safari or Firefox: Safari -> Develop > Show Web Inspector -> Network -> File > Export as HAR. Firefox -> Network tab -> right click -> Save all as HAR.

qa-bot: reminder: attach minimal reproduction steps and OS/browser version (Chrome 114 macOS 12, etc).

kevin (Customer): Uploaded file: 1988-err-har.zip (contains network.har + console.txt). Request id 01H8QWZ2KX-000a, timestamp 2026-03-16T21:12:09Z. Browser: Chrome 114.0.5720. x64 macOS 12.5. 

maya (Support): Received — thanks. Julian/sarah, can you pick up correlation with backend logs for 01H8QWZ2KX-000a? Also, kevin — if we need a curl repro we might ask you to run the sanitized pattern from above and paste the output (no secrets). We'll keep you updated. :thumbsup:

julian (Eng): Got it, searching logs now. If anyone else needs the HAR, I'm saving a copy to the incident folder. I'll post findings here.

sarah (SRE): If we find a 502, try running this to capture response headers quickly from the app endpoint (replace path):

```bash
curl -I -H "X-Request-Id: 01H8QWZ2KX-000a" 'https://app.redwood.inference/flow/complete'
```

maya (Support): Thanks everyone — I'll mark this thread as the customer-facing trail. If we want to escalate to infra, ping @sarah.

julian (Eng): Quick note for the record: if the HAR shows a 504 from upstream we may need to increase backend timeouts or add retry logic in the client. Will report after log lookup.

kevin (Customer): Appreciate the fast help. I'll DM the sanitized HAR to maya if needed.

maya (Support): Closing loop soon, will update with root cause or next steps. :sparkles:
